item.title: AOC tries to laugh off 'crazy' woke era as thing of the past, but conservatives aren't amused
item.description: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez laughed off the "Woke 1" era as "crazy," but critics say Democrats haven't renounced any of their far-left positions.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., dismissed her and other socialist politicians' far-left rhetoric as a thing of the past, but conservative opposition was not persuaded.

ABC's "This Week" host Jon Karl asked Ocasio-Cortez to comment on Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong's controversial past comments — including calling for Thanksgiving to be canceled or for prisons to be abolished — some of which she has tried to backtrack on as she seeks the Democratic nomination in her state.

"I have a local city councilman that has this saying, 'Woke 1 was crazy,'" Ocasio-Cortez said while laughing. "And I think that what’s important is that we have to assess what a candidate is saying now."

This received swift backlash from many conservatives.

ALEXANDRIA OCASIO-CORTEZ SHRUGS OFF PAST 'DEFUND THE POLICE' COMMENTS, JOKING 'WOKE 1 WAS CRAZY'

"It sounds a little desperate to claim that you can't hold a politician accountable for something wacky they said less than six years ago, and a call to cancel Thanksgiving is among the wackiest," Tim Graham, the Executive Editor of NewsBusters at the Media Research Center, wrote in an exclusive statement to Fox News Digital. "Hong has inveighed against not just Thanksgiving, but Valentine's Day, the Fourth of July, and Halloween, and she found Christmas triggering," 

"Once a radical Democrat wins a primary, the party strategists are going to try to make their candidate sound more moderate to voters who don't pay a lot of attention to politics," he added. "So they will try to claim outrageous statements are already out of context and out of date, even if they're not. Tweets like Hong's aren't about policy in 2026, but they can still suggest that her temperament isn't ready for prime time."

Manhattan Institute Vice President and Pollster Jesse Arm spoke to Fox News Digital as well, saying there is one key question Democrats need to answer.

"The obvious question for AOC and her allies is: Which views from ‘Woke 1’ do they actually think were crazy? Sex-change operations for children? Biological men in women’s sports? Race-based discrimination in hiring and admissions? Decriminalizing theft? Refusing to prosecute repeat offenders? Open borders? Debt forgiveness? Banning private health insurance?" he said.

SOCIALIST LEADER SQUIRMS DURING TV INTERVIEW WHEN FORCED TO ADDRESS PUSH TO ABOLISH PRISONS, POLICE

"The problem is that they haven’t renounced any of it — and they don’t intend to," Arm continued. "After voters delivered a pretty decisive rejection of the ideological excesses of early 2020s, many leftist politicians now attempt to laugh off the era as ‘crazy’ without acknowledging their own role in it or identifying which of their substantive positions they now reject."

Arm recalled one key example of how Democrats’ climate alarmism, even in the late 2010s, looked tone-deaf.

"AOC herself provides a revealing example. In 2019, she was telling young people that the world was going to end in 12 years because of climate change. Now she’s talking about starting a family in the 2030s. I’m glad she expects a future," he said. "But it would be nice if the politicians who spent years convincing a generation of young Americans that they had no future would acknowledge that some of the things they said during ‘Woke 1’ weren’t just crazy — they were deeply and dangerously wrong."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Commentators on social media added their takes as well, such as Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, who replied to footage of Ocasio-Cortez's interview by saying, "You don't get to spend years pushing to fundamentally transform the country, divide it on racial lines, inject DEI into every institution, and then try to brush it off as a minor misunderstanding when your worldview turns out to be extremely unpopular with the American people."

"We waged war on woke because ultimately woke represented a war on truth," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis replied. "Now, we have a prominent leftist acknowledging that Florida was right to reject the woke mind virus."

Conservative commentator Ryan James Girdusky quipped, "'Woke 1 was crazy' new cop out for insane positions held as recently as yesterday."

item.title: Fauci in the hot seat as GOP senator tears into 'truly sick' vaccine texts: 'Tip of the iceberg'
item.description: Sen. Ron Johnson says Anthony Fauci's government phone texts reveal he privately feared mRNA vaccines could cause miscarriages in pregnant women.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A Senate Republican leading the charge on investigating Dr. Anthony Fauci’s old government phone told Fox News Digital that the revelation that the former COVID-czar was concerned that vaccines could cause miscarriages was "just the tip of the iceberg."

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., in an interview with Fox News Digital, alleged that the first tranche of texts from Fauci’s old government iPhone was a clear sign that the man who became the face of the nation’s COVID-19 response said one thing privately while taking a different message to the public.

"We tell pregnant women don't even have a glass of wine and yet we coerce them, convince them, sometimes mandated them, to get an experimental gene therapy as early as the first trimester," Johnson said. "This is truly sick."

FAUCI'S HHS IPHONE TURNED OVER TO SENATE INVESTIGATORS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

"And the way this has been — I've known about this for years," he continued. "But finally, because we have a text associated with St. Fauci, it's finally getting the play in the media that it’s been deserving for years."

Johnson and Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., obtained Fauci’s phone from his time as the head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) as part of their broader dive into the former chief medical advisor to the president.

It came as Paul was readying to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress for repeatedly invoking the Fifth Amendment — a gambit he successfully pulled off and has since handed off to the Department of Justice (DOJ).

Johnson, who chairs the Senate Homeland Security Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, released the first tranche of private messages found on the device on Monday.

FAUCI HELD IN CONTEMPT AS COVID CELLPHONE LANDS IN HANDS OF SENATE INVESTIGATORS

That conversation from Jan. 2021 was between Fauci, then-Centers for Disease Control (CDC) Director Dr. Rochelle Walensky and Dr. Vivek Murthy, who would become Surgeon General during the Biden administration.

During the back and forth, Fauci admitted that he had concerns about the impact of mRNA vaccines on pregnant women.

"I asked around a bit more and another issue came up that you need to be aware of," Fauci wrote. "Since many people have significant cytokines storm and fever after the 2nd dose, this theoretically could be associated with miscarriage in the 1st trimester."

Johnson charged that "I've never heard a federal health official admit that about the injections," and noted that cytokines storms were linked with adverse effects to the lungs from vaccination.

"What you have to connect this to is what they were saying publicly, that was contrary to that, but also what they're publishing," Johnson said.

He recalled a study published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021 from Dr. Tom Shimabukoro in June of 2021 after Fauci’s initial concern that found that of 827 pregnancies that were exposed to the mRNA vaccines, 104 had "what they call spontaneous abortions, we would call it miscarriage."

Johnson argued, however, that the numbers were skewed.

"Of the 827 women, 700 got their vaccination or the injection in the third trimester, 127 got them in trimester one and two, which is where the 104 miscarriages occur," Johnson said.

"So the proper percentage is 104 divided by 127, an 82% miscarriage rate with women who got the injection in the first second trimester," he continued. "I mean, that is shocking, and they knew it. They knew it, they're not that stupid. They're just that devious to play with the statistics that way to misinform, to lie to the American public."

Johnson’s investigation of the phone and its trove of information is in its early stages, and the lawmaker is approaching information dumps with caution — he doesn’t want to reveal people’s personal information or even delve into Fauci’s personal life.

His main focus is finding more communications where Fauci said one thing privately, and did another in the public eye.

"This is going to take time, but when my staff saw this, I mean, to me, this immediately impacts public safety, immediately impacts informed consent," Johnson said. "And so I had to get this one out there right away. But there are, I'm sure, way more to come."

"I think this is the tip of the iceberg," he continued.

Fox News Digital did not immediately receive comment from the law firm representing Fauci.

item.title: 22-year-old passenger dies after sudden medical emergency strikes aboard Southwest flight to LA
item.description: Rain McMillan Walmsey, 22, became unresponsive on Southwest Airlines Flight 958 from Dallas to LAX, and his cause of death remains deferred.
item.content:encoded:
A 22-year-old passenger who died after a medical emergency aboard a Southwest Airlines flight bound for Los Angeles has been identified as officials investigate what may have led to his sudden death.

Rain McMillan Walmsey died Aug. 7 after becoming unresponsive aboard Southwest Flight 958 from Dallas to Los Angeles, prompting desperate attempts to save him before the plane landed at Los Angeles International Airport.

Newly released records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner reveal the investigation into Walmsey’s death remains open, and exactly what led to the young passenger’s death remains unclear.

The medical examiner identified Walmsey as a 22-year-old man and listed his place of death as "LAX Southwest plane."

CO-PILOT BECOMES SICK MIDAIR AS CREW ILLNESS REPORTS EMERGE AFTER OVERNIGHT LAYOVER

His cause of death was listed as "deferred," which the medical examiner’s office says means the determination is pending additional investigation. No manner of death has been listed.

Walmsey became unresponsive after experiencing a medical emergency while Flight 958 was en route to Los Angeles, law enforcement sources told NBC Los Angeles. CPR was administered to Walmsey aboard the aircraft, and paramedics responded when the flight arrived at LAX, according to the outlet. He could not be revived and was pronounced dead at the scene.

It remains unclear what type of medical emergency Walmsey experienced.

DELTA FLIGHT FORCED TO DIVERT AFTER PASSENGER GOES INTO LABOR AND DELIVERS BABY MIDAIR

Southwest Airlines confirmed to Fox News Digital that a "medical incident involving a customer" occurred aboard Flight 958 from Dallas to Los Angeles on Friday but did not provide additional details, instead referring further questions to local authorities.

The incident follows other recent cases involving passengers who suffered fatal medical emergencies aboard commercial flights.

In January 2025, 53-year-old Barbara Dipoli of Kansas died aboard an Air France flight from Paris to Boston, with authorities saying preliminary information pointed to a medical episode during the flight.

In June 2024, 8-year-old Sydney Weston became ill and unresponsive aboard a SkyWest flight before the plane diverted to Peoria, Illinois.

That same month, a 41-year-old American passenger died after suffering a severe medical emergency aboard a Fiji Airways flight bound for San Francisco.

item.title: Fauci texts raising theoretical miscarriage concern after COVID vaccine dose spark backlash
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci’s private 2021 discussion of a theoretical miscarriage association drew fierce criticism from Republican lawmakers and officials.
item.content:encoded:
Multiple officials erupted on social media after a Senate committee released text messages Monday showing Dr. Anthony Fauci privately raised a theoretical concern that fever and other reactions after a second COVID-19 vaccine dose could be associated with miscarriage in the first trimester.

The January 2021 conversation, obtained from Fauci's government-issued cellphone, shows the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) discussing concerns about fever and other symptoms following a second vaccine dose. Fauci wrote that the reaction "theoretically could be associated with miscarriage in the 1st trimester."

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., who released the conversation with Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., blasted Fauci on social media.

FAUCI DISCUSSED COVID MRNA VACCINE CONCERNS FOR PREGNANT WOMEN IN TEXT CHAIN RELEASED BY SENATE COMMITTEE

"Once again, Anthony Fauci was saying one thing in public and something completely different in private," Paul said in a post on X. "He was willing to put women and their unborn children at risk instead of admitting that he was wrong about the vaccines that he tried guilting Americans into taking."

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier also blasted the former top health official, accusing him of withholding information that could have put pregnant women and their unborn children at risk.

"Pregnant women were told it was safe! How many women lost babies due to Dr. Fauci's lies," Uthmeier said in a post on X.

Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, R-Ga., took a step further, calling for Fauci's arrest in an ordeal she called "the most infuriating thing."

"Fauci knew Covid shots cause miscarriages. And still forced the shots. Fauci belongs in prison," Greene said in a post on X.

FAUCI'S HHS IPHONE TURNED OVER TO SENATE INVESTIGATORS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

"If a Covid vaccine can kill a baby and cause a miscarriage, then imagine all the other things it can do to you. And Fauci knew it and still told people to take it," she added in a separate post.

Johnson's press release on the text messages said the findings "could have an immediate impact [on] public health and the principle of informed consent."

In addition, Fauci had previously acknowledged that there were "no data or theoretical reason" to believe vaccination earlier in pregnancy should be preferred over vaccination later in pregnancy.

He also noted that more than 10,000 pregnant women had already been vaccinated with "no issues" reported.

Around that time, Dr. Vivek Murthy, who was part of the conversation and would later serve as former President Joe Biden's surgeon general, flagged a World Health Organization recommendation against Moderna's vaccine for pregnant women due to limited data.

Murthy said issuing a strong recommendation against vaccination based on a lack of data could be "potentially quite damaging to public confidence among pregnant women."

Fox News Digital's Eric Mack contributed to this report.

item.title: DiJonai Carrington responds to 'White privilege' post, but leaves meaning of it still unclear
item.description: DiJonai Carrington responded to Emmanuel Acho's critique of her "White privilege" post after her ejection, but still won't clarify what she meant by those words.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Sky’s DiJonai Carrington finally responded to those criticizing her for posting "WHITE PRIVILEGE @indianafever" after being ejected for clotheslining Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham.

But her response still doesn’t explain why she chose those specific words to post on her Threads account, presumably from the locker room, following her ejection during Saturday’s loss to the Fever.

Carrington quote tweeted a retort to ex-NFL player and sports personality Emmanuel Acho, who said on his "Speakeasy" show that Carrington could not call her foul on Cunningham "White privilege."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I’ve never once claimed that the assessment of the foul was white privilege (that was your assumption)," Carrington’s reply to Acho read on X. "Try exercising your critical thinking skills, I know you studied psych.

"Furthermore, I’m the LAST thing from ignorant or asinine when it comes to speaking on 'white privilege,' do ya research on that one. I actually went to school, one of the top universities might I add, to educate myself on this exact subject," Carrington, who attended Stanford for four years before grad-transferring to Baylor, added. "I would never use that term as a rhetorical weapon knowing the historical and social weight it holds without having the proper evidence to substantiate it."

FORMER NFL PLAYERS CALL OUT DIJONAI CARRINGTON FOR BLAMING EJECTION ON 'WHITE PRIVILEGE'

So, if Carrington’s Threads post wasn’t about the assessment of the foul, then what exactly did her Threads post refer to on Saturday night following her ejection?

Fox News Digital didn't immediately receive a response from Carrington’s rep after asking that exact question.

Does Carrington’s post refer to Cunningham, though she didn’t accuse her by name and there was no evidence the foul has any connection to the Fever star’s position on transgender athletes in women’s sports? Does it refer to the Fever organization, or the WNBA as a whole?

Carrington took time to reduce the list of possibilities by one, but for whatever reason, continues to remain vague and mysterious about the controversial post.

The WNBA has yet to announce any discipline for Carrington’s actions in the loss to the Fever, which occurred late in the first quarter when she was hawking Cunningham, who had a breakaway layup. When Cunningham went up, Carrington jumped and smacked her in the face.

Cunningham was livid, getting up from the hardwood and confronting Carrington face-to-face. As she was being held back by teammates, she shoved Carrington slightly before officials stepped in as well.

After official review, Carrington’s foul was upgraded to a Flagrant 2, and she was ejected from the game.

Cunningham has been at the center of a widening political debate about biological men in women’s sports, as supporters of her stance held a fourth rally outside the Fever road game at the United Center in Chicago on Saturday, while counterprotesters also gathered near the venue.

WHO IS DIJONAI CARRINGTON? WNBA STAR WHO SMACKED SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM, GOT EJECTED AND BLAMED 'WHITE PRIVILEGE'

Cunningham has stated she does not harbor any hatred toward transgender people, but she believes protecting girls and women in sports is "common sense." She has received backlash for her belief, and the debate has spilled inside and outside of WNBA venues, while discourse continues online.

Meanwhile, this isn’t the first time Carrington has been at the center of controversy involving Fever players. During the 2024 campaign, where she was playing with the Connecticut Sun, Carrington mocked then-rookie Caitlin Clark for what she believed was flopping and later called Fever supporters "the nastiest fans in the W" after receiving racist abuse from online users.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Then, Carrington struck Clark in the eye while defending a pass during the 2024 WNBA playoffs, leading to the latter having a black eye. Both players said that the contact was accidental, though Carrington drew some renewed criticism after she appeared to joke about the controversy during an Instagram Live video.

Beyond basketball, she has drawn attention for wearing an explicit anti-President Donald Trump sweatshirt and urging WNBA players to oppose Trump administration policies affecting women and the LGBTQ community.

Carrington is in her sixth WNBA season, her first with the Sky, where she is averaging 9.8 points and 2.2 rebounds across her five games in a depth role for Chicago.

Fox News' Jackson Thompson and Matthew Reigle contributed to this report.

item.title: Democratic Michigan AG accuses her party of 'absolutely not' doing enough to counter antisemitism
item.description: Michigan AG Dana Nessel told MS NOW that five Democrats charged with antisemitic acts are still permitted to attend the Michigan Democratic Party convention.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel accused the Michigan Democratic Party on Monday of not doing enough to address antisemitism by allowing members charged with antisemitic acts to still attend the upcoming convention.

Nessel previously told Jewish leaders and community members that she would not attend the convention scheduled for Aug. 29 out of security concerns. As the state's first Jewish attorney general, Nessel told MS NOW that she was familiar with antisemitism while in office, but the Democratic Party has now become intolerant of different ideas.

"Look, myself and other Jewish electeds are subjected to a barrage of antisemitic threats," Nessel said. "And that's been happening literally since my first day in office in 2019, long before Oct. 7. But in addition to that, you know, what we've seen in the Democratic Party as of late in here in Michigan is that we're not seeing the same kind of civil discourse that we used to be able to have and the ability to have a diversity of ideas and opinions that are, you know, respected."

LEFT-WING ACTIVISTS HECKLE PRO-ISRAEL DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS AT MICHIGAN CONVENTION

When asked whether the party was doing enough to counter antisemitism, Nessel replied "absolutely not" and claimed that criminally charged Democrats were still allowed to attend the convention.

"We have five members of the Democratic Party who have been charged with antisemitic acts of vandalism and harassment and threats to other Democratic officials, some of whom are Jewish and including an attack on the Jewish Federation of Detroit," Nessel said. "So those people are still permitted to come to the convention. And it's just baffling to me that while these charges are pending, they're going to be allowed to be there despite, you know, these credible charges against them."

She added, "So I think that there's a lot that we could do. We could enforce a code of conduct that says that, again, you can’t chase people around the convention yelling at them. It’s not appropriate to boo people off the stage even if it’s a candidate whose ideas you don’t support."

JEWISH MICHIGAN DEMOCRATS ADMIT THEY WILL VOTE REPUBLICAN IF ABDUL EL-SAYED BECOMES NOMINEE

In a comment to Fox News Digital, Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said, "We are appalled by the details of this indictment and the hateful, antisemitic threats that took place. The Michigan Democratic Party condemns all acts of hatred and violence, which have no place in Michigan and should not be tolerated."

Another Michigan Democratic Party spokesperson said that the party received a code of conduct complaint but will not comment on pending investigations.

"We are committed to ensuring party-hosted events are safe and secure environments for all attendees. We reject antisemitism, Islamophobia, and all forms of hateful conduct. We are working diligently with stakeholders, elected officials, and party membership to prepare for our August convention and look forward to welcoming Michigan Democrats to the Lansing Center on Aug. 29," the spokesperson said.

FETTERMAN 'DARES' EL-SAYED TO STICK WITH PIKER, CLAIMS MICHIGAN NOMINEE HAS 'LITTLE MAN SYNDROME ENERGY'

During the interview, Nessel also addressed Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, whose campaign has been embroiled in antisemitic controversies based on his past comments. Though she did not explicitly endorse El-Sayed, Nessel told MS NOW that she has no desire to see GOP candidate Mike Rogers win the Senate seat and that she plans on speaking with El-Sayed about her concerns soon.

"First of all, I’d like him to tone down his rhetoric a little bit," Nessel said. "And what I mean by that is, AIPAC — which many of us do not support or agree with — and Israel, with many of us who do not support or agree with their government or the actions of Benjamin Netanyahu, they cannot be the central villain in literally every story."

She continued, "If we’re talking about reforming healthcare, which all of us want to do in the party, it’s not AIPAC that is responsible for those problems, it’s the health insurance and pharmaceutical companies," adding, "Not everything is about AIPAC, not everything is about Israel."

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for comment.

item.title: Inside CFP expansion battle as SEC, Big Ten and TV networks fight for College Football’s next big move
item.description: College Football Playoff expansion hinges on whether the SEC and Big Ten can agree on a format, with financial models driving the December decision.
item.content:encoded:
A December deadline is looming for the College Football Playoff committee to make a decision on the future of expansion for the postseason tournament to crown a national champion.

While there has been plenty of discussion around whether the CFP should expand beyond twelve teams starting in 2027, the question is more centered around how much additional revenue adding a new batch of teams would bring to the conferences.

On Monday, leaders from conferences across the sport, along with Notre Dame, met virtually to discuss financial models that would give them a better sense around how much money additional games would bring each member school.

Big Ten's Tony Petitti Makes It Clear To SEC: Agree To 24-Team CFP Expansion Or Format Stays At 12

Maybe one of the more important questions should center around what's best for the sport. But, we all know that money is the driving force behind any type of expansion that could happen in the future.

After the SEC and Big Ten, who hold a majority stake in these talks, could not come to an agreement on whether it should be a 24 or 16 team playoff moving forward, the topic was tabled until this off-season.

Yes, the Big Ten has been a vocal proponent of adding an additional twelve-teams to the playoff. At the same time, SEC leaders have been pushing for a 16-team playoff, which would only open a certain amount of games that competing networks of ESPN could bid on in the future.

ESPN IS REPORTEDLY PREVENTING THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF FROM EXPANDING TO 24 TEAMS

I would guess it's fairly easy to see why the Big Ten would want an increase in teams, which is supported by the ACC and Big 12, seeing that it would allow FOX and others to submit bids for the additional inventory.

On their virtual call Monday, there was not a lot of conversation about what a future format would look like , according to sources. But, those intense discussions are coming, especially over the next few months, as a deadline looms.

Remember, there doesn’t need to be a formal discussion regarding the future for ideas to be floated among member schools. All it takes is a phone call or email to gauge the interest of conferences.

Also remember, anything over fourteen games would trigger a clause in the CFP agreement allowing others to join the party from a television network standpoint.

But, only two years into the twelve-team playoff, the push for expansion has drawn unwanted backlash from college football fans. Why mess with something that isn’t broken, or so brand new that we have yet to see its full potential?

SEC commissioner Greg Sankey, at the behest of his bosses within the conference, has continued to harp on the problems with getting out of contracts for its SEC championship game. In fairness, the conference has a plethora of sponsors that spend a lot of money on advertising the annual game in Atlanta at Mercedes Benz Stadium.

The SEC’s High-Stakes Destin Showdown Over CFP Expansion, NIL And A Possible NCAA Breakaway

If the conference were to align with the Big Ten and other 24-team proponents, they have to know that's it is financially worth the jump. Also, while we've been trending this way for the past few seasons, getting rid of a conference title game is not the most popular move.

Even if the game is starting to lose its luster, or any type of benefit for the college football playoff, it's obviously still an important financial marker for the conference. And while the Big Ten, ACC or Big 12 might be in agreement about moving forward without these conference title games, they still have to persuade the SEC to join their movement.

As we've previously reported, there has been talk of turning conference championship weekend into a 'play-in' scenario.

But now, with a push from current CFP rights holder ESPN, a new 20-team format is being discussed among committee members, though that conversation did not make its way onto the virtual meeting that took place Monday, according to sources.

It would technically be a 16-team playoff, but with four different play-in games that would determine which additional teams join the field.

Think of it in the same light as the NCAA Tournament's 'first four in' bonanza that took place annually in Dayton, Ohio, before the organization decided to increase the amount of teams who received a bid.

While this might sound appeasing to some, the Big Ten is not onboard with this idea, sources told OutKick-FOX News and others.

In reality, this feels like if we are going to ultimately see the CFP expanded, there has to be enough financial reasons for a conference like the SEC to agree.

And, don't forget that the current right's holder, ESPN, would rather continue sublicensing games to networks like TNT so that they would still be in control of the television agreement.

Well, we thought there could be something in the works towards the end of the last season when committee members met in Miami before the national championship game.

All sides are arguing over what the future should look like, which will also determine how much money each conference would made from additional games.

THE FIGHT: NIL ARMS RACE FUELING NEW PUSH FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF EXPANSION

Right now, December is the hard-deadline put into place by ESPN for an agreement on expanding the College Football Playoff.

Also, with the SEC and Big Ten being given a majority vote over other conferences like the ACC, Big 12 and Group of Six, getting the two biggest conferences in college athletics to agree on a format is no easy task.

Don't expect a decision any time soon, meaning in the next two months. This entire process is complex, as the financial ramifications will ultimately dictate where we head in the future.

There are plenty of college football fans hoping this argument extends past the deadline, so that we continue to having a twelve-team field.

But unfortunately, the power of money will be the ultimate dictator in where we are headed in the future.

When is it not in college athletics?

item.title: ‘Common sense against crazy’: Trump-backed candidate sounds alarm on socialist Hong in Wisconsin race
item.description: Tom Tiffany and Glenn Youngkin warn that democratic socialist Francesca Hong's policies on defunding police and abolishing prisons threaten Wisconsin.
item.content:encoded:
OCONOMOWOC, Wis. - Rep. Tom Tiffany, who is expected to win Tuesday's Republican gubernatorial primary in Wisconsin, is warning voters that a likely general-election match up with socialist state Rep. Francesca Hong could determine whether socialism gains a foothold in the Midwestern battleground state.

Tiffany, speaking to Fox News Digital alongside former Virginia Gov. Glenn Youngkin, said on the eve of the primary that the election could determine whether Wisconsin becomes a "firewall" against the spread of socialism as far-left candidates continue to topple more moderate Democrats in high-profile primary elections this spring and summer.

"Is the heartland going to be the firewall that stops this movement of socialism coming from, especially the East Coast?" Tiffany said. "And I think Wisconsin will be. We’ll be the place that stops socialism."

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

Hong is the polling frontrunner in a Democratic gubernatorial nomination showdown that's been rocked this summer after two major contenders dropped out, and another candidate re-entered the race.

A member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), the 37-year-old former chef and single mother is backed by top nationally known progressives, including Reps. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota and Ro Khanna of California, a potential 2028 Democratic presidential contender

Hong is running on a platform that includes guaranteed paid leave, boosting the state's minimum wage from $7.25 to $20 per hour, and a one-year moratorium in Wisconsin on building AI data centers. Her "TAX THE RICH" plan proposes raising state income taxes by 1% for couples making over $431,000 and individuals making over $323,000.

Hong has faced scrutiny over years-old social media posts calling for defunding and abolishing the police. But she says she no longer supports cutting police budgets or abolishing police departments. 

MEET THE FAR LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN THE 2026 MIDTERMS

"I'm not defunding the police, not abolishing police. I am serious about public safety," Hong emphasized on Saturday as she took questions from voters.

"I think what Francesca Hong stands for is the antithesis of America," Youngkin said. "She wants to defund police, close prisons. She wants to get rid of the military. She wants to get rid of the presidency. I mean, these are all the things that the DSA stands for and she is a card-carrying member."

"[Tiffany] is what's gonna be on the ballot against someone who literally wants to deconstruct America," Youngkin said.

"This is what this election eventually is gonna be about — common sense against crazy."

Youngkin and Tiffany spoke with Fox News after holding a campaign event at a new home development in this outer western suburb of Milwaukee, where Tiffany unveiled his "Unlocking Homeownership in Wisconsin" agenda.

"I just know my friends and neighbors, including some who are Democrats, they are not crazy," Tiffany said. "They do not believe in some of these crazy policies, abolish prisons, abolish police, highest tax rates that you could possibly have. I mean they do not accept that."

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15 MILLION WAR ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

Past social media posts from Hong have drawn scrutiny, including a 2021 post stating that police "exist to uphold white supremacy" and posts calling to abolish the U.S. Senate and criticizing Thanksgiving and Valentine’s Day.

Hong walked back her Thanksgiving comments, amid backlash, and now says that Thanksgiving is her "favorite holiday."

On her resurfaced tweets, Hong told reporters on Saturday that she had "evolved" and "learned."

But Tiffany told Fox News ,"[They are] going to do everything they can to walk them back, but people see through this. Those flip-flops, people know about that already and they're going to know about it as we go through the final, you know, couple months of the campaign. They see through that type of stuff when you are not genuine."

When asked by Fox News Digital to respond to Tiffany's criticism by Fox News Digital, Hong characterized her past posts as some "bad takes."

"You have some hot takes, sometimes bad takes on Twitter," Hong said about the posts, as she spoke with reporters following a campaign stop in Sun Prairie, Wisconsin. "And I let my feelings out into the world."

SPEAKER JOHNSON TURNS DEMOCRATS’ SOCIALIST CIVIL WAR INTO NEW WEAPON FOR MIDTERMS

Republicans, like Tiffany and Youngkin, have sought to portray Hong’s progressive record as a liability for the battleground state.

"This is a moment for the heartland of America to stand up for America," Youngkin said of the race.

Tiffany, a hard-right member of the conservative House Freedom Caucus and a former dairy farmer who is endorsed by President Donald Trump, emphasized, "Some people may not agree with a few of the policies that I'm for, but they know I'm genuine. They know I'm authentic."

Hong has argued that Democratic voters are fed up with the party establishment, claiming her candidacy appeals to a variety of both Democrats and Republicans, who disagree with Trump and his aligned candidates.

Tiffany and Hong enter Tuesday as the frontrunners in their respective primaries, with Tiffany running against medical service technician Andrew Manske, and Hong facing off against three other Democratic candidates — Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who is backed by retiring Democratic Gov. Tony Evers, former Wisconsin Department of Administration secretary Joel Brennan, and democratic state Sen. Kelda Roys.

item.title: Record-setting El Capitan rock climber dies at age 30 in Sierra Nevada accident
item.description: Jake Whisenant, 30, has died after an accident in the Sierra Nevada. The well-known rock climber once scaled El Capitan’s Nose route twice in a single day.
item.content:encoded:
An accomplished rock climber who set a speed record on one of Yosemite's famed El Capitan routes recently died in an accident in California's Sierra Nevada.

Jake Whisenant, age 30, died on Aug. 3, according to the Tulare County Sheriff's Office Coroner Division. 

Authorities haven't disclosed the circumstances of his death — but it was listed as an accident.

His death was announced by Bailee Moore, who described Whisenant as her "lifelong friend and confidant."

NURSE IMPALED BY POLE DURING HIKE FORCED TO TREK 10 MILES FOR HELP: 'A FREAK THING'

Moore wrote that her heart was "impossibly heavy" as she shared the news.

"Our family is absolutely devastated by this news but find solace in the fact that Jake died doing what he loves in the beautiful Sierra Nevada," said Moore.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Tulare County Sheriff's Office for additional comment.

YELLOWSTONE OFFICIALS DECIDE FATE OF BISON THAT LAUNCHED GRANDFATHER 8 FEET IN AIR

Whisenant had made a name for himself in Yosemite’s climbing community with a series of impressive feats on El Capitan, one of the most challenging places to rock-climb.

Whisenant climbed El Capitan's Nose route twice in a single day in May with fellow climber Noah Fox, finishing in 14 hours and 38 minutes, according to the Yosemite Climbing Association.

In October 2024, Whisenant and climber Brant Hysell set a speed record on El Capitan's Lurking Fear route, completing the climb in 2 hours, 55 minutes and 32 seconds.

At the time, Whisenant described it as a "truly magical day that I’ll never forget."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

item.title: Brad Pitt admits he began drinking again after years of sobriety
item.description: Brad Pitt tells Esquire he got "back off the wagon" after seven years sober and describes the one period he says he understood suicide as relief.
item.content:encoded:
After seven years of sobriety, Brad Pitt started drinking again.

The startling confession came as Pitt reflected on his darkest moments, the lasting scars of grief and the complicated reality of struggling despite having "won the lottery" in life.

"I was sober for seven years. And then I got back off the wagon," Pitt told Esquire for the September cover story.

COUNTRY SINGER RUSTON KELLY COMMITS TO SOBRIETY AFTER RELAPSING ON DRUGS FOLLOWING FREAK GOLF CART CRASH

The actor said he approached drinking differently after giving up his sobriety, describing his consumption as more limited than before. "In a more restrained manner," he clarified. "I got overconfident a couple times, went, ‘Yep, nope, not good for me. Not in big quantities.’"

Pitt’s candid admission came as he reflected on the harder chapters of his life and acknowledged that fame and success had not insulated him from struggle. The "F1" star has been dealing with "family stuff" since 2016, when he began the divorce process from his ex-wife, Angelina Jolie.

Pitt’s reflections took a darker turn as he recalled a period when the pain became nearly unbearable.

"I was never suicidal in any way. It just was not my makeup," he told the outlet. "In fact, if I have any afflictions, it’s probably being a congenital optimist. Which has helped many times, and it’s also gotten me – I’ve walked foolishly head-on into a Mack truck because of my optimism. Or, as my forever-funny friend David Fincher will say, 'Yeah, you see the glass as half full, but it’s half full of urine.' Anyway, I’ve never been suicidal except for one little period."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"And in that one little period, I just thought – I just couldn’t – just didn’t see a way out," Pitt continued. "The pain was so oppressive that – I wasn’t going to act on this, but I could feel – I could feel the cold steel of the bullet in my head, and it felt like relief. And I thought, Oh, okay, now I understand – I understand suicide, in the sense that it’s just relief. It’s just looking for relief from the pain. But I also think we have incredible survival instincts. And for me, that immediately kicked in, but it was just... "

The Oscar winner tempered his candid admission by acknowledging the extraordinary hand he had been dealt in life.

"Yeah. Like, listen: This s--t ain’t easy," he said. "And you’re talking to a guy who won the lottery."

Pitt also reflected on the lasting impact of grief, describing the pain it left behind alongside an unexpected sense of beauty.

"Grief, if you survive it, leaves a gaping hole, but it also leaves profound beauty," he said. "It’s an aching beauty, but it’s beauty."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Pitt first gained major attention with his memorable supporting turn in 1991’s "Thelma & Louise," before becoming a leading man in films including "A River Runs Through It," "Legends of the Fall" and "Se7en."

His signature films include "Fight Club," "Ocean’s Eleven," "The Curious Case of Benjamin Button," "Moneyball" and "Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood."

Pitt has also built an influential career behind the camera through his production company, Plan B Entertainment. As a producer, he won the best picture Oscar for "12 Years a Slave," adding to a résumé that extends well beyond acting.

Now in his 60s, Pitt looked back on the previous decade with a sense of urgency.

"God, I want my fifties back," he said. "I would do more. Your fifties are just – man, anything that’s on your mind, go. Go attack it. Go attack it now."

item.title: Mamdani clashes with Democratic Socialists' push to abolish police and prisons
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended police, prisons and jails on air, distancing his administration from the DSA's abolition platform.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended police, prisons and jails during a Friday appearance on "The Clay Cane Show," putting distance between his administration and the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) platform as political streamer Steven Bonnell, known online as "Destiny," told Fox News Digital that Mamdani would likely govern moderately while helping more radical candidates gain power.

Bonnell said Mamdani’s control of a prominent and politically secure office could allow him to build support for other socialist lawmakers without implementing the DSA’s most radical proposals himself.

"I think that Mamdani holds a very powerful, very safe office where he can be entrenched for a long time in order to ‘hold the door open’ for other, (arguably) more radical lawmakers in the future," he said.

HARRIS REACHES OUT TO SOCIALIST MAYOR MAMDANI IN LATEST SIGN SHE'S SHORING UP SUPPORT FOR POSSIBLE 2028 BID

Mamdani addressed his differences with the DSA after host Clay Cane noted that the organization's platform calls for abolishing institutions including prisons, the Senate and the presidency.

"I would say, especially when it comes to public safety, I've been very clear that we have our police force, we have prisons, we have jails [and] the purpose of these is also to ensure that we are delivering safety and justice hand in hand. And what that means is that New Yorkers need not choose between the two," Mamdani said.

He also credited the NYPD with driving down violent crime while emphasizing that public safety should not come at the expense of justice.

"I am proud of our police department for their work in delivering the lowest levels of murders and shootings and even the number of shooting victims in recorded history over seven months over this year," Mamdani said.

MAMDANI WALKS BACK PLAN TO INCREASE NYPD HEADCOUNT FOLLOWING DSA PRESSURE

The NYPD reported 381 shooting incidents, 462 shooting victims and 149 murders during the first seven months of 2026, the lowest record totals for that period. Major crime declined 6.6% compared with the same period in 2025.

The position contrasted with the DSA's official platform, which describes defunding law enforcement and weakening police unions as steps toward eliminating police and prisons.

DSA co-chair Megan Romer defended the organization's approach to police and prisons during an interview with New Yorker editor David Remnick Monday on "The New Yorker Radio Hour." Romer rejected eliminating law enforcement, while defining defunding as redirecting department money into social programs.

"I am not in favor of getting rid of police entirely tomorrow," Romer said. "I think it means taking funding back and moving it elsewhere, right?"

"It's not communities with cops on every corner. It's communities that have good schools, good jobs, good park systems, good recreation for their teenagers, things like that," she added.

DSA CO-CHAIR PUSHES BACK ON SOVIET UNION COMPARISONS, WANTS PRISONS TO BE 'LESS NECESSARY'

Bonnell predicted to Fox News Digital that the demands of running the nation’s largest city would keep Mamdani from applying the DSA’s policies, even as the mayor used his popularity to promote other socialists.

"As someone who has to actually govern, though, I don't see him applying any of the more radical DSA positions," he said. "Rather, he'll govern moderately, remain decently popular, market well, then use that position and popularity to promote others."

Republican New York City Councilwoman Vickie Paladino's office told Fox News Digital that Mamdani’s remarks were intended to obscure an agenda that remained central to the DSA.

"Mamdani is politically savvy and understands that DSA messaging on police and prison abolition has been embarrassing and deeply problematic for Democrat candidates heading into the midterms," Paladino said. "As the top DSA figure in the country, he’s trying to deploy some smokescreen on behalf of the party, nothing more."

"Make no mistake, abolishing police and prisons is now a baseline policy position for the DSA, regardless of what Mamdani is saying at the moment," she added.

Despite distancing his administration from that platform, Mamdani praised NYC-DSA during the interview for helping elect minority candidates.

"And I think to me, one thing I've appreciated about New York City DSA is that it has been one of the engines behind the creation of a new generation of Black and Brown leadership, the likes [of which] we haven't seen in quite some time," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani’s office, the national DSA and NYC-DSA for comment on whether the mayor’s position conflicts with the organization’s platform, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Child vaccine schedule reduced as Trump moves to dramatically shift medical power to parents
item.description: President Donald Trump signed an executive order recommending childhood vaccines for 11 diseases instead of the CDC's 18, separating the MMR shot.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump is spearheading a major overhaul of current childhood vaccination mandates in an effort to give parents more freedom to choose which shots their children take, and when.

Trump signed an Executive Order announcing what the administration is calling the Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations, saying that not only do the new recommendations align with other developed nations, but they also with common sense.

A memo on the order recommends children receive immunizations for 11 diseases, fewer than the 18 current Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidelines. It also ended recommendations that all minors receive the COVID-19 jab.

A Health and Human Services (HHS) scientific assessment compared the U.S. vaccine schedule to those of peer nations in Europe. It found that the American childhood vaccine schedule recommends many more vaccines than most western nation counterparts — sometimes close to double the number of shots.

SWITZERLAND FIRES HOCKEY COACH WHO ADMITTED TO FAKING VACCINATION STATUS FOR 2022 BEIJING OLYMPICS

The memo recommends that parents should have five separate vaccine appointments, instead of children taking all of the vaccines at once.

"I think you're going to see some amazing results [by] breaking it up," Trump said in the Oval Office while announcing the order on Monday.

"It's not just that you're doing fewer vaccines or jabs, as they say, but you're doing them in a series of visits to the doctor. Much smaller amounts."

Trump has previously voiced opposition to appointments where babies and toddlers are given multiple vaccinations at one time.

The memo on Trump's latest health-related executive action stresses flexibility for parents, urging them to "make individualized decisions for higher-risk children through shared clinical decision-making."

The memo also recommends separating the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccines into separate shots, instead of taking all three vaccines at once, as is common. It also notes that the U.S. is in the minority of peer nations that mandates vaccinations in order for children to enroll in school.

Additionally, the order focuses on discriminatory practices based on vaccine status.

"In addition, this executive order directs the Attorney General to advance legal challenges against states that violate children's rights to religious or medical vaccination exemptions," Trump said.

"Parents can still choose to give their children all of the vaccinations if they wish, it's up to the parents — we're making recommendations that are strong – but it's up to the parents if they wish and they will be covered by insurance," he continued. "However, this updated recommendation finally aligns the United States with other advanced and developed nations around the world. More importantly, it aligns us with common sense and knowledge."

LONGER LIVES, WORSE HEALTH? SCIENTISTS UNCOVER TROUBLING TREND ACROSS GENERATIONS

The order is part of Trump's commitment to Make America Healthy Again (MAHA). Last year, the president, by executive order, launched the MAHA Commission, aimed at addressing the causes of what the administration says is an "escalating" health crises.

The commission was specifically directed to investigate childhood chronic diseases. The probe led to "a sweeping plan with more than 120 initiatives to reverse the failed policies that fueled America’s childhood chronic disease epidemic."

The White House did not provide further comment when reached about the latest initiative.

item.title: Trump demands Iran compensate Americans and protesters after Tehran seeks war reparations
item.description: President Donald Trump demands Iran compensate families of USS Cole victims and thousands killed by Iranian-backed attacks in future negotiations.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Monday demanded that Iran compensate Americans killed or seriously wounded in attacks he blamed on Tehran, while also calling for payments to the families of Iranian protesters killed by the regime.

The president also said he had instructed his representatives to raise his compensation demands in any future negotiations with Iran.

Trump’s remarks came after senior Iranian officials demanded compensation from Washington as part of Tehran’s conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

"I see that Representatives of the Islamic Republic of Iran are asking for compensation for the damage done to them during the last five month Military Conflict (started because, THEY WILL NOT HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON), even though it was never mentioned in any of our negotiations or meetings!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN WILL PAY — WHAT IT TAKES TO END THE WAR REMAINS UNCLEAR

Trump also called Iran’s request for compensation "an interesting idea" before saying he was also demanding compensation from Iran, "for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts, for which they are famous, as led initially by General Soleimani, including the families of those killed on the USS Cole, and thousands of others killed in combat."

"Additionally, compensation should be paid to the families of the hundreds of thousands of innocent protestors that Iran has killed over the last 50 years, not to mention the 52,000 that have been killed in the last five months," he wrote.

"I have instructed my representatives to put this firmly into any and all future negotiations," Trump wrote.

TRADE VESSEL STRUCK BY PROJECTILE IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ AMID US-IRAN TALKS

In a second Truth Social post, Trump said Iran should also be held responsible for "the damages and death caused to the people of Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza."

Following his two posts, Trump revisited the topic during an executive order signing at the White House and confirmed that Tehran had demanded "reparations."

"They asked for reparations, you might say," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

"Or they asked for money for the damage that we've done. I said that's a good idea. Well, we're going to ask for money for the damage they've done over a 50-year period," he said.

INVESTIGATORS BELIEVE IRANIAN HACKERS ARE LIKELY BEHIND CYBERATTACK ON MINNESOTA WATER SYSTEMS: REPORT

Trump added: "So, if there are damages to be paid, I think Iran should pay those damages."

Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said over the weekend that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the United States "corrects its behavior," setting out a series of conditions for reopening the strategic waterway.

Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, also set out conditions for reopening the strait, including an end to U.S. military operations and threats, the lifting of sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian assets and compensation for war damage, according to reports.

"The Supreme National Security Council will never back down, whether in war or in negotiations," Zolghadr said.

On Aug. 8, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Iran and Oman were "very close" to reaching a deal on a new shipping route through the strait, but also said there would be conditions, including compensation for what Tehran says were U.S. violations of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MOU), Reuters reported.

TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE

Trump on Monday also declined to say whether Iran had exhausted its chances to reach a deal with the United States, telling reporters at the White House, "You'll find out."

When asked whether the last round of talks was Tehran’s last chance before decapitation strikes, Trump said, "You'll find out, you'll find out."

"Well, we have that certainly that ability if we want to do that. Yeah. You'll find out," he repeated.

Trump also said Sunday that the United States was "only semi-negotiating" with Iran.

item.title: Georgia jogger runs for her life after stranger allegedly tries to mow her down 3 times
item.description: Jesse Allen Davis allegedly tried to run down a woman three times at a Cobb County apartment complex after she greeted him during her morning workout.
item.content:encoded:
A Georgia woman out for a Sunday morning workout was allegedly forced to run for her life after a stranger tried to mow her down three times moments after she offered him a simple greeting.

The terrifying encounter unfolded at the Sedgefield Apartments in Cobb County on July 19, where the woman was walking and exercising when she crossed paths with Jesse Allen Davis, 21, according to a criminal warrant obtained by Fox News Digital.

The woman did not know Davis, but the two exchanged what authorities described in the warrant as a "brief, polite greeting."

WASHINGTON DRIVER CHASES BOY ON DIRT BIKE DOWN SIDEWALK, GETS HIT WITH MULTIPLE CHARGES

item.title: Joe Scarborough goes scorched earth on Democrats not separating themselves from Hasan Piker
item.description: Joe Scarborough blasts Democrats as "too woke" to condemn Hasan Piker's rhetoric after ally Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate primary race.
item.content:encoded:
MS NOW "Morning Joe" host Joe Scarborough launched a blistering attack on far-left streamer Hasan Piker and Democrats unwilling to distance themselves from his rhetoric Monday, warning the party risked repeating what he viewed as its costly 2024 mistakes after Piker ally Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Democratic Senate nomination.

Scarborough, raising his voice and shouting at times, said Democrats were "too woke to call out the obvious" and questioned why party leaders were reluctant to draw a line over Piker's past comments about rape during Hamas' Oct. 7 terrorist attack, when he remarked that it didn't matter to him if it occurred.

"This is about the Democrats once again, fumbling the football on the two-yard line when they have a chance to make great gains, but being so woke, I don't know if you want to call it woke 1, woke 2, or woke 3, but being too woke to call out the obvious!" Scarborough yelled. "I swear to God. It's really, it's crazy that we're even having this conversation."

The Republican National Committee (RNC) has sought to turn El-Sayed's continued relationship with Piker into a general election liability. RNC national spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre told Fox News Digital Sunday that Democrats' unwillingness to disavow the streamer reflected a broader problem for the party.

MARK HALPERIN CALLS HASAN PIKER A 'HORRIBLE PERSON' AS DEMOCRATS FACE PRESSURE TO DISTANCE FROM STREAMER

"El-Sayed is a terrorist sympathizer and an America-hating socialist. His refusal to distance himself from Hamas-hugging radicals like Hasan Piker reaffirms his true allegiance is to terrorist groups, not America. Democrats' refusal to disavow this clown shows they either share his poisonous ideology or they're too cowardly to confront it," Baldassarre said.

"The Democrat Party is being driven off [a] cliff by socialists who are driving blindfolded while arguing about the view. Unless Democrats hit the brakes, every candidate on the ballot will have to answer for socialists’ outrageous beliefs that will bankrupt our country and strip every American of safety, sanity, and freedom," she added.

Scarborough specifically called on Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., to demand that candidates distance themselves from such rhetoric.

"If somebody says, a woman being raped doesn't matter in the grand scheme of things, it's OK to call that person out and demand that candidates distance themselves from those people!" Scarborough shouted.

FETTERMAN 'DARES' EL-SAYED TO STICK WITH PIKER, CLAIMS MICHIGAN NOMINEE HAS 'LITTLE MAN SYNDROME ENERGY'

The fight has intensified since El-Sayed narrowly defeated establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. El-Sayed will face Republican Mike Rogers for the seat held by retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

Piker made repeated appearances with El-Sayed, including at a Detroit pool party the night before the primary. El-Sayed has rejected Piker's most controversial remarks but resisted calls to sever ties.

"Of course I oppose rape. Of course I don't think 9/11 was justified," El-Sayed said during an April appearance on "Fox & Friends." "[Just] because you appear with somebody, doesn't mean you agree with them on everything."

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., has also challenged El-Sayed to maintain the relationship now that he must appeal beyond Democratic primary voters.

JOHNSON TURNS DEMOCRATS’ SOCIALIST CIVIL WAR INTO NEW WEAPON FOR MIDTERMS

"I dare you to continue to campaign with people like Hasan Piker because he now will quickly find out it’s easy to campaign in the echo chamber as a Democrat," Fetterman told Fox News Digital.

Piker has pushed Democrats in the opposite direction, calling for party members who refuse to support El-Sayed to be "punished," while centrist Democratic group Third Way recently announced a $15 million campaign aimed at weakening the Democratic Socialists of America's influence.

Scarborough said the debate reminded him of Democrats' failure to recognize cultural issues that hurt them during the 2024 election.

"Why are we bringing this up now? We're bringing this up now because it seems an awful lot like what was happening in 2024 when Democrats couldn't get out of their own way to win an election they should have won," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the DNC, El-Sayed, Piker and Schumer for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Former NFL players call out DiJonai Carrington for blaming ejection on 'white privilege'
item.description: Emmanuel Acho and Breiden Fehoko push back after Dijonai Carrington posted "white privilege" following her ejection for flagrant fouling Sophie Cunningham.
item.content:encoded:
Two former NFL players agree that Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington further impeded racial progress in America by basically blaming her ejection on Saturday on "white privilege."

"This is a prime example of why we can't ever move forward as a country," former NFL player Breiden Fehoko wrote on X about Carrington's accusation.

"For every person who liked this bullsh*t and is encouraging this victim-a** mentality, you should be ashamed. It's honestly sad how far we've drifted as a country."

For background, Carrington hard-fouled Fever forward Sophie Cunningham on Saturday on a play that more closely resembled a clothesline than a play on the ball. Carrington left Cunningham bloodied in the mouth. She was rightfully called for a Flagrant 2 and ejected from the game.

Moments later, Carrington posted "white privilege" on Threads from the locker room, as if racism was the reason for her ejection.

EX-ESPN HOST SAYS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DESERVED TO BE EJECTED AND PUNISHED — NOT DIJONAI CARRINGTON, WHO CLOTHESLINED HER

Former NFL player and podcaster Emmanuel Acho also pushed back on the claim.

"DiJonai Carrington posted ‘White Privilege’ from the locker room after being ejected for fouling Indiana Fever’s Sophie Cunningham," Acho wrote on X, reacting to a screenshot of Carrington’s post. "Judge for yourself, but color didn’t have nothing to do with the flagrant 2. IMO."

He continued on his podcast:

"Can we stick to basketball for a moment? She flagrantly hit Sophie Cunningham in the head ... the refs made the right call."

"Now, I'd be remiss if I didn't mention .. this was not a race-based decision. To call that a white privilege-based foul is to completely undermine the term of white privilege and to also completely ignore the rules in basketball. You hit her in the head. You drew blood. You didn’t connect with the ball at all whatsoever.

"So to me, it was just very ignorant and, to some degree, asinine by D.J. Carrington to suggest that that call was based on white privilege. Have we seen examples of white players make that same foul and get away with it? Have we seen examples of black players make that same foul and get away with it? Yes. There was no white privilege involved in that specific call."

Well said.

You can watch the full segment from Acho here.

WNBA FACES DISCIPLINE DILEMMA AFTER CARRINGTON'S 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' POST TARGETING INDIANA FEVER

While Acho and Fehoko are covering the matter honestly and with reason, most of the media is not. Earlier on Monday, OutKick documented some of the most cringeworthy remarks in defense of Carrington.

Most notably, former ESPN anchor Cindy Brunson argued that Sophie Cunningham was the one who deserved to be ejected – not Carrington, who clotheslined her.

You read that correctly.

Elsewhere, the WNBA pregame shows on NBC and ESPN have avoided discussing Carrington's post. In fact, NBC host Maria Taylor didn't just ignore it, but accused those criticizing Carrington of injecting her into the "culture war," as if she played no role in doing so.

The race-lady duo of Jemele Hill and Cari Champion also, predictably, rushed to Carrington's defense.

As we explained, members of the sports media cannot bring themselves to cede an inch of ground in the culture war. That means never, under any circumstances, criticizing a black lesbian in defense of a straight white woman.

Good for Acho and Fehoko for not subscribing to this worldview.

Carrington deserved to be ejected. She deserves to be suspended. And neither has anything to do with race.

item.title: 100 Kodiak driverless trucks are headed for public roads
item.description: Atlas Energy Solutions plans to grow its Kodiak driverless truck fleet from 28 to 100 by mid-2027, with public highway driving in Texas and New Mexico.
item.content:encoded:
Atlas Energy Solutions is expanding its fleet of Kodiak-powered driverless trucks across Texas and New Mexico. The trucks already haul sand to oil and gas well sites without anyone inside the cab.

Now, Atlas and Kodiak plan to grow the fleet from 28 driverless trucks to 100 by mid-2027. They also expect the trucks to begin operating on public roads in early 2027. However, that timeline still depends on operational milestones.

The expansion gives us a clearer look at how driverless trucking could move from private industrial roads onto highways.

Join us Saturday, Aug. 29, at 10 a.m. ET for a free CyberGuy LIVE class covering five simple steps to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.

Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.

NEW YORK SCHOOL PAUSES HUMANOID CLASSROOM ROBOT PILOT PROGRAM

Atlas previously operated its driverless trucks from one load-out location at a time. It now runs them simultaneously from two depots about 90 minutes apart. One site is in Texas while the other is in New Mexico. The wider footprint lets Atlas reach more well sites across the Permian Basin. It can also respond faster when customers need more sand delivered. The operation connects with Atlas' 42-mile Dune Express conveyor system. That system moves sand closer to the well sites before the trucks complete the final portion of the trip.

Don Burnette, founder and CEO of Kodiak, said the two companies have built the world's largest fleet of driverless big-rig trucks: "Together, Atlas and Kodiak have deployed the world's largest fleet of driverless big-rig trucks. We've demonstrated that autonomous trucking is delivering meaningful results today. Our expanding partnership, which now covers two unique locations, is creating a blueprint for how autonomy can transform logistics by improving efficiency, increasing productivity, and delivering lasting value for customers at commercial scale."

As of March 31, 2026, Atlas's driverless program operated 28 driverless trucks across 15 routes. Those trucks had carried about 7,000 loads and hauled more than 450,000 tons of sand. The fleet also logged more than 23,500 driverless operating hours during the first quarter of 2026. On July 20, Kodiak-powered trucks delivered 176 loads in one day. The companies called it a daily record for the 18-month deployment.

Earlier in 2026, Kodiak and Atlas also introduced a driverless truck that can pull three connected trailers. The combined loaded weight tops 135 tons. That kind of load would grab anyone's attention. It also raises an obvious question. What happens when these trucks leave private roads and begin driving beside the rest of us?

Kodiak plans to launch driverless highway operations by the end of 2026. Atlas expects its Kodiak-equipped fleet to follow onto public highways in 2027. The company is not alone in moving toward humanless highway freight. A separate autonomous truck recently completed a 230-mile commercial delivery in Texas with nobody in the cab.

Burnette told CyberGuy that other motorists should not expect unusual behavior from Kodiak-powered trucks: "Kodiak-powered trucks already operate autonomously on highways across the southern United States with a safety driver in the cab to oversee the system.The Kodiak Driver is engineered to be a safe and cautious driver and to follow normal driving etiquette, so other motorists should not notice anything unusual."

That may sound reassuring. Still, most drivers will want more than a smooth lane change before they feel comfortable beside a truck with no human behind the wheel. CyberGuy recently took a closer look at whether autonomous trucks can make highways safer, including Kodiak's arguments about fatigue, distracted driving and real-world testing.

The Permian Basin can be brutal on vehicles. Trucks can face triple-digit temperatures, dust storms, sudden flooding and high crosswinds. Dense morning fog can also make visibility difficult. Kodiak equips its trucks with a sensor suite built around cameras, with radar and lidar support. These systems give the truck a detailed view of the surrounding environment.

However, more sensors cannot make every condition safe. Burnette said the truck will stop instead of pushing through dangerous weather: "And if conditions aren't safe, the truck won't keep driving. It slows down and safely pulls over." Kodiak says its system responds to construction zones and emergency vehicles as part of normal driving. It also adjusts to changing road conditions. Severe fog or other hazardous weather can still stop an autonomous trip. According to Burnette, Kodiak-powered vehicles will remain parked when conditions become unsafe.

AI KILL SWITCH BILL COULD SHUT DOWN ROGUE MODELS

A damaged component or communications failure can create a serious problem in any large truck. The stakes may feel even higher when nobody is sitting in the cab. Burnette said the Kodiak Driver checks both the truck and its autonomous system while it operates: "The Kodiak Driver continuously monitors the truck and its autonomous driving system. If it detects a critical problem, such as a mechanical, sensor or communications failure, it can execute a fallback maneuver that safely pulls the truck out of traffic and brings it to a stop in a safe location."

According to Burnette, "The health and safety of all trucks are overseen by Kodiak's command center, and a human can remotely provide assistance should a truck need additional help."

Kodiak also cites a safety evaluation from Nauto, an AI-powered fleet safety company. The Kodiak Driver earned a VERA safety score of 98 out of 100. That result tied for the highest score among more than 1,000 commercial fleets in Nauto's network. The other fleets used human drivers. The system earned a perfect score for inattentive driving and high-risk driving. It also earned 100 for traffic violations. Its aggressive driving score was 95. You can read CyberGuy's full breakdown of the Kodiak Driver's independent safety score. Burnette pointed to the evaluation in his response: "We are proud that an independent evaluation by Nauto, a leader in AI-powered fleet safety technology, gave Kodiak the highest score in a safety study, tying for first place and outperforming 1,000 human-driven fleets."

Driverless trucks create another concern that has nothing to do with rain or road debris. A connected vehicle can become a cybersecurity target. Kodiak does not publicly detail every safeguard. Publishing a complete security blueprint could help attackers. Burnette said Kodiak treats cybersecurity as part of its safety work: "Cybersecurity is something we take extremely seriously because safety starts long before a truck ever reaches the road."

He said Kodiak uses multiple security layers and continuously watches for suspicious activity. The company also tightly limits access to its systems. "We build multiple layers of security into our vehicles and systems to help protect against unauthorized access, and we continuously monitor for unusual activity. For security reasons, we don't discuss the specific safeguards we use or how they're implemented. But access to the systems is tightly controlled and if it detects something unusual, it will bring itself to a safe stop rather than continuing to operate." Kodiak's public technology materials say the company isolates safety-critical functions from external communication ports. It also says it protects vehicle infrastructure with end-to-end encryption.

You probably will not wake up tomorrow and find every delivery truck driving itself. Early public deployments will likely focus on routes where operators already understand the conditions. Still, the Atlas expansion shows that fully driverless trucking has entered commercial service. These trucks are already working without a person in the cab.

The next major step will bring them onto roads used by commuters and families. Other truck drivers will also begin sharing lanes with autonomous rigs. For you, the biggest issue is how the system responds when normal driving suddenly becomes abnormal. Dangerous weather can change a trip in seconds. So can equipment failures, cyberattacks or unpredictable motorists.

Kodiak says its system will reduce speed and move toward a safe stop when conditions become unsafe. Human teams will also monitor the fleet through a command center. The technology could eventually affect deliveries and transportation costs. It may also change trucking jobs, an issue CyberGuy explored in a closer look at whether autonomous trucks could replace drivers by 2027.

As these vehicles reach public highways, transparency will become even more important. Drivers deserve clear information about crash reporting and emergency response. They also need to understand the limits of remote assistance. Regulators will need to test company safety claims against real-world results. A strong safety score provides a starting point, but public trust will depend on consistent performance over time.

OUR ENEMIES FOUND A WEAKNESS IN ESSENTIAL TECHNOLOGY. WE MUST FIX IT … FAST

Kodiak and Atlas are rapidly expanding a commercial driverless truck operation that already moves heavy loads without anyone in the cab. The plan to grow from 28 trucks to 100 by mid-2027 shows how quickly autonomous trucking can scale inside a demanding industrial environment. Public highway use will bring a new level of scrutiny. Drivers will want answers about severe weather, system failures, public-road emergencies and cybersecurity. Kodiak says its trucks can stop when something goes wrong. Human teams also remain available through a command center. However, the technology must prove that those protections work reliably as more trucks enter service. The expansion could reshape how companies transport essential materials. Yet public trust will depend on what happens when these trucks encounter the unpredictable moments every driver knows too well.

Would you feel comfortable driving beside a 135-ton truck with no one in the cab if the company said its AI could handle the unexpected? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: 3 things to avoid in middle age could mean 13 more years without dementia, study finds
item.description: NYU Langone Health research reveals how avoiding high blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking in midlife could add nearly 13 dementia-free years.
item.content:encoded:
Middle-aged adults who manage to avoid high blood pressure, diabetes and smoking can gain nearly 13 additional years of life free from dementia, according to new research led by NYU Langone Health.

The study, published in the journal Neurology Open Access, analyzed long-term health data to determine how midlife cardiovascular wellness shapes brain function decades later.

Minimizing these three common vascular threats between ages 48 and 68 dramatically postpones mental decline, according to the research.

ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TESTS MAY PREDICT SYMPTOMS YEARS IN ADVANCE, BUT EXPERTS URGE CAUTION

"Our findings argue that people need to actively avert these factors in midlife as a strategy for preserving brain health for more than a decade," said Dr. Josef Coresh, the study’s senior investigator and founding director of the Optimal Aging Institute at NYU Langone, in a press release.

Identifying actionable ways to stall memory loss is vital, he said, pointing out that roughly 42% of Americans are projected to develop dementia after turning 55.

The reviewed data came from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study, an ongoing trial that began in 1986. It included a cohort of more than 12,000 dementia-free participants whose average age was 56.

POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY HELP PROTECT AGAINST A DEADLY DISEASE, DOCTOR SAYS

After screening subjects for smoking habits, elevated blood pressure and diabetes, researchers tracked their health trajectories for an average of 26 years.

By the end of the observation window, 3,008 participants had developed dementia, while 5,238 died without cognitive impairment.

The study revealed a significant gap based on midlife health: Participants who avoided all three risk factors averaged 30 dementia-free years following their baseline exams. In contrast, those with all three conditions averaged just 17 years before developing dementia or dying.

Demographic trends were reported across sex and race. Female participants had longer periods of cognitive health than male participants, regardless of health risks.

Among subjects with all three risk factors, women survived an average of 18.1 years without dementia, compared to 16.6 years for men.

White participants with all three risk factors averaged 19.6 dementia-free years, while Black participants facing the same health profile averaged 16.0 years.

"These results suggest that vascular risk reduction may benefit all groups, but that certain populations, such as Black adults, may especially benefit from targeted prevention efforts," Coresh said, expressing hope that the data will motivate people to quit smoking and monitor cardiovascular health starting in their late 40s.

The authors noted several limitations to their findings, including that the observational design cannot prove direct cause and effect.
